title: Fabric Kit Manual
content: ## 1\. COMPONENTS ### **Please identify and confirm the following components.** ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054560874/mceclip0.png) ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054560894/mceclip1.png) **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)SCALE** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)UTILITY KNIFE** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)SCREWDRIVER** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)CHARGING ADAPTER** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)USER MANUAL** ## 2\. TOOL LEGEND ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png) **BENDING TEST DEVICE** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561034/mceclip2.png)** ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png) **STRETCH TEST DEVICE** ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561014/mceclip0.png) ## 3\. SPECIFICATION ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561154/mceclip3.png) ## 4\. HOW TO ATTACH THE DIGITAL FORCE GAUGE TO THE FABRIC KIT ### **Use total of eight screws to assemble. Remaining two screws are extra.** **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561354/mceclip5.png)Screw the Jig into the Digital Force Gauge. Turn about 3-4 times and do not tighten all the way. However screw the Jig until the Control Lever faces up, aligning with the Digital Force Gauge.** **![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428853/mceclip4.png)** **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428933/mceclip6.png)Align the Holder underneath the Digital Force Gauge. ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428973/mceclip7.png) Fasten the Holder to the Digital Force Gauge with Screws (x4). ** **![mceclip8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561414/mceclip8.png)** **![mceclip9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561434/mceclip9.png)Loosely tighten the Screws (x4) to affix the Digital Force Gauge to the Fabric Kit, enough so that Digital Force Gauge can be moved.** **![mceclip10.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561454/mceclip10.png)** **![mceclip11.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429013/mceclip11.png) Shift the Digital Force Gauge to align the Jig as the image below vertically.** **![mceclip12.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561474/mceclip12.png)** **![mceclip13.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561494/mceclip13.png) Tighten Screw B to affix the Digital Force Gauge Holder to the Fabric Kit. ****If the Digital Force Gauge is not affixed properly, the measured Force values may not be accurate.** ## 5\. OVERVIEW **Prepare fabrics![mceclip14.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561694/mceclip14.png) Measure the fabric weight and thickness ![mceclip14.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561694/mceclip14.png) Measure the bending strength ![mceclip14.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561694/mceclip14.png) Measure the stretch ![mceclip14.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561694/mceclip14.png) Calculate entered measurements ![mceclip14.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561694/mceclip14.png) Apply a texture** ## 6\. HOW TO MAKE FABRIC ### **Launch CLO Enterprise, then switch to Emulator mode using the top-right drop-down menu to enter the values measured from the Fabric Kit.** #### ** A. SWATCH PREPARATION ** **![mceclip17.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429393/mceclip17.png)Before cutting out the swatches, please ironing the swatch gently without causing any shrinkage.** **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561354/mceclip5.png) Confirm the grainline of the fabric.** **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428933/mceclip6.png) Prepare a total of three swatches with the provided stencil. ****** **![mceclip15.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561754/mceclip15.png) Each swatch will represent a different grain, cut in the (1) weft, (2) warp, and (3) bias directions, measuring 220mm x 30mm in size.** **![mceclip15.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561754/mceclip15.png) These will be used to measure the weight, bending, and stretch properties of the fabric.** **![mceclip16.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561774/mceclip16.png)** **![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428973/mceclip7.png) Cut the swatches along the drawn guidelines, being as precise as possible for accurate measurements. ****** #### **B. FABRIC WEIGHT** **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561354/mceclip5.png) Turn on the scale.** **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428933/mceclip6.png) Place all three swatches on the scale. ****** **![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428973/mceclip7.png) Enter the displayed weight in the Emulator. ** **![mceclip18.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561794/mceclip18.png)** #### **C. FABRIC THICKNESS** **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561354/mceclip5.png) Press the lever of the thickness gauge to create a gap and place the swatch.** **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428933/mceclip6.png) Place the 220mm x 30mm swatch in between the gap. ****** **![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428973/mceclip7.png) Release the lever and enter the measured thickness to the Emulator. ** **![mceclip9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561434/mceclip9.png) Click Next to continue. ** **![mceclip19.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561834/mceclip19.png)** #### **D. BENDING TEST** **The Bending Test is performed 3 times : first for the weft swatch, and next the warp swatch, then the last for the bias swatch.** **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561354/mceclip5.png) Slide open the 1-1 Ruler of the Bending Test device.** **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428933/mceclip6.png) Turn the 1-2 Clamp back, then insert the end of the swatch, lining it up to the dotted line. ****** **![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428973/mceclip7.png) Pull down the 1-2 Clamp to affix the swatch. ** **![mceclip20.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561914/mceclip20.png)** **![mceclip9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561434/mceclip9.png) Wind the 1-4 Control Lever clockwise, then stop when the fabric hits the ground. ** **![mceclip21.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429453/mceclip21.png)** **![mceclip11.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429013/mceclip11.png) Measure and enter this point of contact as the Contact Distance (A). ** **![mceclip13.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561494/mceclip13.png) Place the 1-1 Ruler beneath the swatch, then enter the measured length (B) in the Emulator. ** **![mceclip22.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561954/mceclip22.png)** #### **E. STRETCH TEST** **The stretch test will allow you to measure the stretchability and threshold at which a fabric will no longer stretch. To do this you will explore the relationship between length of stretch and force applied to the fabric, then record and input your findings into the Emulator Mode of CLO.** **The reading from the Length Ruler and Digital Force Gauge combined will be one set of measurements. You will need a minimum of 3 sets and a maximum of 5 sets for each swatch.** **When testing, you will need to determine, which unit of length will be your constant.** ![mceclip23.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429513/mceclip23.png) **![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561354/mceclip5.png) Wind the Control Lever until the needle aligns with 0 on the Length Ruler.** **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428933/mceclip6.png) Loosen the Clamps at each end of the Fabric Bed. ****** **![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428973/mceclip7.png) Insert both ends of the swatch between the Jig openings, aligning the 10mm line marks. ** **![mceclip9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561434/mceclip9.png) Tighten the Clamps at each end to secure the swatch ends.** **![mceclip11.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429013/mceclip11.png) Turn on the Digital Force Gauge. ****** **![mceclip13.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561494/mceclip13.png) Determine Length constant: ** **![mceclip17.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429393/mceclip17.png) We recommend you to fill out all five sections as possible because when you have more measurements, data is more accurate.** **![mceclip15.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561754/mceclip15.png)When the swatch is pulled by 1mm and the force is less than 0.01kgf** **1) Pull the fabric swatch until the force value is 0.01kgf. 2) Starting with the length reached at step 1, check the length and force of each 10mm increment. 3) Record 10 sections. (In the case of not being able to record 10 sections, record all the measurable sections.) 4) Use a value only when the force difference of each section is at least 0.02kgf. (If the force difference for each interval is less than 0.02kgf, do not use that value.) 5) Finally, select and use values resulted in at least 3 sections and up to 5 sections. (We recommend that you fill out all five sections as much as possible because the more measurements you have, the more accurate the data is.).** **![mceclip15.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054561754/mceclip15.png)When the swatch is pulled by 1 mm and the force value is over 0.01kgf** **1) Check the value of the force when the swatch is pulled to 1mm. 2) Starting with the length reached at step 1, check the length and force of each 1mm increments. 3) At this time, measure 3 to 5 sections. (We recommend that you ll out all ve sections as much as possible because the more measurements you have, the more accurate the data is)** **![mceclip24.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054563194/mceclip24.png) Once the test has been completed for a swatch, reset the Control Lever so the needle aligns with 0 on the Length Ruler. Then unscrew the clamp at each end and remove the swatch. If you are finished testing you can turn the Digital Force Gauge off. In between each swatch test you should turn the digital force gauge off and then back on after the needle has been returned to the 0 marks. ****** **![mceclip25.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055429673/mceclip25.png) Click Next to Continue. ** ## 7\. HOW TO USE THE DIGITAL FORCE GAUGE **The Digital Force Gauge uses the default settings as the image below. If a button was mistakenly pushed, power the Digital Force Gauge off, then on, to reset the device to its default settings. However, if the default unit of measurement was changed, press button B to reset the device to Kgf.** **![mceclip27.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054563294/mceclip27.png)** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)FREQUENTLY USED BUTTONS** **A. POWER** \- **turn the Digital Force Gauge on/off** **C. LED - turn the LED display on/off** **D. UNIT - change the unit of measurement; Kgf is used to measure the stretch** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)FREQUENTLY USED BUTTONS** **The following buttons are not used in the Stretch Test.** **If one of these buttons are mistakenly pushed, reset the Digital Force Gauge with the Power button.** **B. RESET** **E. MODE** **F. REVIEW ****G. SETTINGS I. SAVE** **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360055428333/mceclip2.png)CHARGING** **Use the provided adapter to charge the Digital Force Gauge.**
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for identifying, assembling, and utilizing the components of the Fabric Kit and Digital Force Gauge for accurate fabric testing and measurement.

title: Render in CLOSET
content: **Render in CLOSET ** **-** Render 3D Garments in CLOSET regardless of user’s computer specification. \- Main Menu▶Render ▶**Render via CLOSET** \- Main Menu▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360010223033/mceclip0.png)Share▶**Render via CLOSET** \- Main Menu▶File▶ Share ▶ **Render via CLOSET** \- You are navigated to CLOSET.

title: Reset Bounding Volumes (ver4.2.0)
content: **Objective** Reset Bounding Volumes to the original placement after adjustments. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Bounding Volume ▶ ![____10.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003078947/____10.png) **Reset Bounding Volumes** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Bounding Volume ▶ ![____10.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003078947/____10.png) **Reset Bounding Volumes** → Bounding Volumes are replaced to their original placements.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users in resetting bounding volumes to their original placements within the Avatar Editor of Clo3D.

title: 3D Garment Information (ver4.1.0 and Above)
content: **List of Contents** Enter Default Garment Information Add Category Reorder Category Delete Category **Objective** Write and check important Garment information. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Information ▶ **Garment** ** Operation** **Enter Default Garment Information** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Information ▶ **Garment** → The Garment Information window appears. → Four categories: StyleNumber, Name, Description, Fabric, Colorway, and Size appear by default. 2. Click the ![edit_configurator.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000717328/edit_configurator.png) **Edit** icon on the right top corner of the window. → The Garment Information window changed to the edit mode. 3. Type in necessary information next to each category and click **OK**. → Typed in information is saved. **Add Category** 1. Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. 2. Click the ![plus_button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000717348/plus_button.png) **Add** icon. → A category is added. Click the drop-down menu and select desired category. → There are eleven categories to choose from: StyleNumber, Name, Description, Fabric, Colorway, Size, Category, Memo, SizeMemo, Price, and SizeChart. 3. Type in necessary information for each category and click **OK**. → Typed in information is saved. **Reorder Category** 1. Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode.. 2. Click and drag the category to the desired position. → The category is moved to where the mouse is released. 3. When categories are re-ordered completely, click **OK**. → Revised category order is saved. **Delete Category** 1. Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. 2. Click the ![____16.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000728667/____16.png) **Delete** icon next to each category. → The selected category is deleted. 3. When the editing is completed, click **OK**. → The deleted category no longer appears in the Garment Information window. **※ Note: ** * Toggle on **Display When Garment File Loads** option to open the Garment Information window every time the file opens. * Open or save Garment information such as categories, order, and contents by using the **![open.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000717468/open.png)Open** and **![save.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000717528/save.png)Save** buttons on the right top corner of the edit mode. * Use the [Default File setting](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002563607-%EA%B8%B0%EB%B3%B8-%ED%8C%8C%EC%9D%BC-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95) to designate default Garment Information file. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for managing garment information, including adding, reordering, and deleting categories to ensure accurate and organized garment data entry.

title: Edit 2D Seam Allowance Properties
content: **List of Contents** Seam Allowance Properties Edit Seam Allowance Properties **Seam Allowance Properties **\- Edit properties of seam allowances as needed. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Seam Allowance** \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026411067/mceclip0.png) **Seam Allowance** tool from the 2D toolbar. ** Edit Seam Allowance Properties ** \- Select the Pattern outline or the Internal Line of the seam allowance to be edited. \- The seam allowance is selected and its Pattern outline or Internal Line is highlighted. \- The selected seam allowance’s properties appear in the Property Editor. * **Width** \- Modify the width of the seam allowance as needed. * **Seam Type** \- Choose the seam type of a seam allowance’s start, end, and intersection. \- Options are activated or deactivated depending on the selected point. * **Start** \- This option activates when only one seam allowance is created on either end of the selected segment. \- Choose the desired type of the seam among three options. * **End** \- This option activates when only one seam allowance is created on either end of the selected segment. \- Choose the desired type of the seam among three options. * **Intersection** \- This option activates when seam allowances are created on both ends of the selected segment. \- Choose the desired type of the seam among six options. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for editing seam allowance properties in 2D pattern design.

title: V-Ray Render
content: **List of Contents** V-Ray Render Interactive Render Stop Render Final Render (Image/Video) **V-Ray Render ** \- Produce more vivid and photorealistic images with clear seamlines and puckerings. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select Render ▶**Render ** \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Window ▶ **Render** ** Interactive Render ** \- By default, the ![stop_render.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025910647/stop_render.png) **Stop Render** tool is activated when the Render window opens. \- Click the ![interactive_render.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025949628/interactive_render.png) **Interactive Render** tool on the 2D toolbar or click the message, “Click here to start the Interactive Render” to start rendering. \- Render Garments and Avatars in the 3D window in real-time with the Interactive Render tool. \- Any changes in 3D view are also reflected in the Render window. **Stop Render ** \- Click the ![stop_render.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025910647/stop_render.png) **Stop Render** tool to temporarily pause while rendering. \- Rendering is paused in the Render window. \- Any changes in the 3D window do not reflect in the Render window when the ![stop_render.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025910647/stop_render.png) **Stop Render** tool is activated. \- Click the ![interactive_render.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025949628/interactive_render.png) **Interactive Render** tool to resume real time rendering. **Final Render (Image/Video) ** \- The image shown in the Render window is a preview of real time Render, which Render settings are not fully applied. \- To extract the final Render images or a video with Render settings fully applied, click the ![final_render.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025910747/final_render.png) **Final Render (Image/Video)** tool. \- The progress of the rendering appears on the right top corner of the Render toolbar. \- When rendering is completed, the Information window appears, informing the images or video have been saved. \- Select the **Open the Folder** button to open the folder where the final output is saved. \- The final output is automatically saved to the saving path assigned in the **Image/Video Properties.** \- **Image/Video Properties** , **Light Properties** , and**Render Properties** are fully applied to the final render output. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on utilizing V-Ray for rendering vivid and photorealistic images and videos, detailing the processes for interactive, stop, and final rendering.

title: Pressure
content: **List of Contents** Pressure Set Pressure **Pressure** \- Assign Pressure to Patterns to express inflated Garments/accessories such as padded jumpers, balloons, pillows, and cushions. \- Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Pressure** ** Set Pressure** \- Using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022740708/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool, select the Pattern to be edited. \- Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Pressure.** \- When the Pressure value is positive, the Pressure is applied to the back of the fabric, but when the Pressure value is negative, the Pressure is applied to the front of the fabric. \- Assign values to Pressure so that the outside Pattern’s Pressure value is 10 and the inside Pattern’s value is -10. Be mindful that the absolute value for two Patterns should be the same. \- When the **Simulation** is activated, the Patterns will inflate. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a guide for assigning and managing pressure settings in garment simulation to create realistic inflated effects for padded items and accessories.

title: Lock All Patterns
content: **Lock All Patterns** \- Lock all Patterns to inhibit selecting and editing in the 2D window and easily select and edit Internal Lines. \- Right-click on the 2D window and select **Lock All Patterns** from the pop-up menu. All Patterns will turn grey and be deactivated. \- Only activated Internal Lines can be selected and edited. **Lock Selected Patterns_ver5.0.0 and Above** \- Select the ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360021137913/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern** or the ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360021137933/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. \- Right click on the Pattern to be locked and select **Lock Pattern** from the right-click pop-up menu. \- The selected Pattern and all Internal Lines within are locked and cannot be selected. \- The selected Pattern and Internal Lines turn grey. \- To unlock the Pattern, right click on the 2D window and select **Unlock All Pattern Outlines.**
content_description: This web page provides instructions on how to lock and unlock patterns in the 2D window to streamline the selection and editing of internal lines in your design workflow.

title: Focus Zoom
content: **Focus Zoom** \- Zoom to the selected Pattern and control the 3D window fiducial to the selected Pattern. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022315187/mceclip1.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar. Right-click on the Pattern or the object and select **Focus Zoom** from the pop-up menu. \- Or, select the Pattern or the object and then hit the F key on the keyboard. \- The 3D window will adjust automatically to zoom to the selected Pattern and the 3D window will be controlled based on the selected Pattern.
content_description: The Focus Zoom feature allows users to effortlessly zoom in on a selected pattern and control the 3D window for enhanced visibility and precision in design.

title: Delete All Curve Points
content: **Delete All Curve Points** \- Delete all curve points on a segment. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021855507/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a segment and select **Delete All Curve Point** from the pop-up menu. \- All curve points on the selected segment will be deleted.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for users on how to delete all curve points from a selected segment in the 2D window using the Edit Curve Point tool.

title: Arrangement Property Setting
content: **Objective** Set arrangement property details once arranging patterns with Arrangement Points. **Location** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024671748/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** ▶ Select 3D Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ **Arrangement ** **※ Note:** The arrangement properties are only accessible to Patterns that are arranged by Arrangement Points. **Operation** 1. [Arrange Pattern with Arrangement Points](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001999287) 2. Follow the indicated guideline: 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024671748/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** ▶ Select 3D Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ **Arrangement** **Point Name** | Shows which arrangement point the selected pattern is on top of. ---|--- **Shape Style** | Changes the arrangement bounding volume pattern to be flat of curved. **Position X** | Moves horizontally according to the arrangement bounding volume. **Position Y** | Moves vertically according to the arrangement bounding volume. **Offset** | Adjusts the offset and curvature between the arrangement bounding volume and the pattern. **Orientation** | Changes the pattern's direction according to the arrangement bounding volume.
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on setting arrangement properties for 3D patterns using Arrangement Points in the Property Editor.

title: Guide for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment
content: **List of Contents** Guideline for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment 1\. Set up on Server PC 2\. Set up on Client PC **Guide for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment** **Objective** Set up CLO 3D/Marvelous Designer Network Version on the Internet environment. Note that you do not need to follow the set-up guidelines below when a Server PC and Client PC are under the same local network environment. Simply plugging the dongle key into a Server PC enables you to run CLO 3D or Marvelous Designer on any PCs under the same local network as the Server PC located without any extra settings. **1\. Set-up on Server PC** **Operation** 1. **Plug the dongle key in the Server PC and install the HASP Driver. ** HASP Driver gets automatically installed during the software installation. However if any trouble occurs during the process or in case of Server only being connected with the dongle key, HASP Driver should be installed manually. [Guideline for Sentinel HASP Driver Manual Installation ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000558507) 2. **Make sure Port 1947 is open in the firewall. ** Port 1947 should automatically be opened once the HASP Driver gets installed however, occasionally it fails to open the port in certain PCs. In this case, go to the firewall settings and open the port manually. Port 1947 is being used for communication between the Client PC and dongle key in the Server PC in order to get an authentication. Setting methods varies considerably in the types of firewall, therefore please ask for support from your network manager. 3. **Make sure the local IP address of the Server is static. (Local IP is dynamically allocated Intranet IP by the router.) ** The local IP address gets changed when the router is restarted if the local IP is not set in static status. To avoid repetitive IP reset in the process, 'port forwarding', set your Server's local IP as 'static'. 4. **Port-forward Port 1947 for TCP and UDP of the Server's local IP in the router setting. ** Port-forwarding enables to transmit the data from Client/Server to Server/Client through Port 1947. Port-forwarding method varies considerably in the types of router therefore please ask for support from your network manager. **※ Note:** <http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_forwarding> [ http://www.wikihow.com/Set-up-Port-Forwarding-on-a-Router](http://www.wikihow.com/Set-up-Port-Forwarding-on-a-Router) **2\. Set-up on Client PC** **Operation** 1. Run CLO 3D/Marvelous Designer Network Version installer. 2. Make sure Port 1947 is open in the firewall.** ** Port 1947 should automatically be opened once the HASP Driver gets installed however, occasionally it fails to open the port in certain PCs. In this case, go to the firewall settings and open the port manually. Port 1947 is being used for communication between the Client PC and the dongle key in the Server PC in order to get an authentication. Setting methods varies considerably in the types of firewall, therefore please ask for support from your network manager. 3. Set external IP of the Server on the dongle key configuration to let the software reaches the Server for an authentication. ** ** This can be done through Sentinel Admin Control Center which is automatically installed during the HASP Driver installation. Access to [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/) Click on 'Configuration' (the red box) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000785828/Clinet_1.png) 4. Click on the third tab called 'Access to Remote License Managers'. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000737807/Clinet_2.png) 5. Make sure to check on 'Aggressive Search for Remote License' and to type the Server PC's external IP in 'Specify Search Parameters' (note that the external IP is different from the local IP mentioned in the 'Set-up on Server PC'). You are able to see the external IP of the Server PC on the website ([http://www.whatismyip.com/](http://www.whatismyip.com/)). ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000785808/Clinet_3.png) Go Back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for setting up the CLO 3D/Marvelous Designer Network Version in an Internet environment, detailing the necessary steps for both server and client PCs.

title: [2D Tool] 1:N Segment Sewing
content: **Objective** Easily sew multiple segments (N) to a single segment (1.) If the total length of N segments and the length of 1 segment are different, the 1 segment is equally divided by the number of N segments. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶**Segment Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290728/_______.png) **Segment Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Segment Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290728/_______.png) **Segment Sewing** 2. Select a single segment which multiple segments are sewn to. 3. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, drag the mouse to hover over the N segments. Before clicking the segment, be careful to make Directional Notches parallel to each other. 5. Then, click on the segments to establish Sewing Lines on the N segments. 6. Release the Shift key to complete the 1:N Segment Sewing. **※ Note** * While establishing 1:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the sewing line cannot be applied. * While establishing N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for easily sewing multiple segments to a single segment in the Clo3D software, ensuring precise alignment and functionality in the sewing process.

title: CLO-SET CONNECT LINK

Select the tool/menu indicated. → The parent category of CLO-SET CONNECT appears in the folder list. 2. Check the desired purchase folder. → Sales items appear. 3. Click the Account at the top right. → The Account window appears. → By default, the CLO-SET CONNECT account is linked to the corresponding CLO account. 3. title: Edit Curvature
content: **Edit Curvature ** * **Edit Curvature ** \- Convert a straight line to a curve or edit the curvature of a curve. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021884827/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curvature** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Curvature** * **Convert a Straight Line to a Curve \- **Click and drag a part of a straight line. \- The straight line will be converted to a curved line. * **Edit the Curvature of a Curve ** \- Click and drag the curve created with the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021891727/mceclip1.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool or the AI Bezier Curve method. \- The curve will be exaggerated or moderated.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a concise guide on using the Edit Curvature tool to convert straight lines to curves and modify existing curves in your design workflow.

title: Free Sewing
content: **List of Contents** Free Sewing Create Free Sewing Directional Notch **Free Sewing** \- Freely create Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022454888/mceclip0.png) **Free Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Sewing ▶ **Free Sewing** ** Create Free Sewing** \- Four clicks are needed to create a pair of Free Sewing Lines. * **Freehand Sewing** \- Navigate to the 2D window and hover over the Pattern outline or the Internal Line where the Sewing Line should be created. A blue point will follow along the mouse cursor. \- Click on the Pattern outline or the Internal Line to start the Sewing Line. Drag the mouse cursor to designate the direction. Then, click again to complete the first half of the Sewing Line. \- Create the second half of the Sewing Line as above. When click and dragging the mouse cursor after establishing the start point, a blue point will appear to guide the length of the first half of the Sewing Line. Click again to complete the second half of the Sewing Line. * **Create Sewing with Designated Value** \- While click and dragging the mouse cursor after establishing the start point, right-click to access the create Sewing Line window. \- Type in the desired value and select OK. \- When the length of the Sewing Line is designated, the end point of the Sewing Line will be created automatically. **Directional Notch** \- The Directional Notch’s position alters depending on the movement of the mouse cursor. \- To reset the Directional Notch of the first half of the Sewing, you must cancel the action and restart. \- To cancel the first half of the Sewing Line, hit the Esc key or the Ctrl+Z keys on the keyboard. \- To reset the Directional Notch of the second half, cancel the action before creating the end point and recreate the Sewing Line. \- To cancel the second half of the Sewing Line, hit the Delete key or the Backspace key on the keyboard. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Free Sewing tool and creating directional notches in sewing pattern design, offering step-by-step instructions for users.

title: Edit Curve Point
content: **List of Contents** Edit Curve Point Edit Free Curve Points Add Free Curve Points to Free Curves Delete Free Curve Points **Edit Curve Point** \- Add and edit free curve points on segments. \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021960108/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve point** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Curve Point.** ** Edit Free Curve Points ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021960108/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window and click on a segment to add a curve point. \- Click and drag the added curve point to edit the curvature. \- Or, click and drag the segment to add and edit the curvature simultaneously. \- Select and move multiple Curve Points at once. While moving the Curve Points, right click to type in desired Distance Moved (ver.4.2.0). **Add Free Curve Points to Free Curves** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021960108/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- When a curve point is added to a free curve, the curve will be modified based on the added curve point. **Delete Free Curve Points ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021960108/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Select the curve point and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. \- The selected curve point will be deleted. \- Select and delete multiple Curve Points at once(ver.4.2.0). Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides comprehensive instructions for editing, adding, and deleting free curve points in the 2D pattern design tool.

title: Offset as Internal Line along Curve
content: **List of Contents** Offset as Internal Line along Curve Number of Offsets Offset Distance to Segment Edge Straight Line Perpendicular Direction **Offset as Internal Line along Curve** \- Create Internal Lines between two Pattern outlines along their curve. \- Select two lines and right click to access the pop-up menu. Then, select **Offset as Internal Line along Curve.** \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447008/mceclip0.png) **Edit Pattern** tool, select two lines which Internal Lines will offset In between. Then, right-click and select **Offset as Internal Line along Curve.** \- The Offset as Internal Line along Curve window will appear. ** Number of Offsets** \- Set how many Internal Lines will be created in between the selected lines. **Offset** \- Set the distance between the offset Internal Lines. **Distance to Segment Edge** \- Set how far the offset Internal Lines will apart from the Pattern outline. * **Reverse Direction ** \- Horizontally reverse the Internal Lines’ position based on the Di"stance to Segment Edge. * **Opposite Segment** \- Vertically reverse the Internal Lines’ position based on the Distance to Segment Edge. **Straight Line** \- Create offset Internal Lines as straight lines. **Perpendicular Direction** \- The offset Internal Lines will be created perpendicular to the Pattern outlines. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on creating internal lines along curves in pattern design, detailing the offset settings and options available for customization.

title: Invert Selection
content: **Invert Selection** \- Invert the Pattern selection, selecting the Patterns currently not selected. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021445568/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021388307/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window and right click on the desired Pattern to select Invert Selection from the pop-up menu. \- The selection will be inverted, selecting the ones that are not currently selected.
content_description: This web page is designed to guide users on how to invert their pattern selections in the 2D window of CLO 3D, allowing them to easily select unselected patterns.

title: [Property] Create Button Texture
content: ### **Objective** Create and apply custom textures to buttons in CLO in order to express various button styles. * UV maps for each default button are included in the CLO Asset Library as photoshop files. * The files can be opened and edited in Adobe Photoshop to apply custom textures and logos to the existing button shapes. * When UV maps are used, all images or type will increase or decrease in size when the button width, ligne, or thickness are changed in CLO. **Operation** 1. Download UV maps of buttons from the [Library window](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000527827-Library-Window). ![Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360081953953/Button.png) 2. Locate the asset folder on your computer. (**PC:** C:\Users\Public\Documents\CLO\Assets / **MAC:** User/Library/Application Support/CLO) **※ Note:** on PC you can right click on the folder name in CLO Library and choose “Copy the path”. Then you can paste this path location into a file browser to locate it. 3. Open .psd file in Adobe Photoshop. There are 4 types of layouts that UV maps will have. ![UV.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360081938953/UV.png) 4. Each part has a separate layer with a shape defining the section that needs to be filled or covered. 5. An image can be placed/embedded or a pattern [Define](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/using/creating-patterns.html) and filled to cover the desired location. Type can allose be added. 6. Hide UV outlines and Text layers, then save the image. **※ Note:** Saving the image in .jpeg format is recommended. 7. Open the custom saved UV map through the Texture section of the[ button property](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115006020988--Style-Property-Apply-Custom-Button-Texture).
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and applying custom textures to buttons in CLO, utilizing UV maps available in the CLO Asset Library for enhanced button styling.

title: Guide for Installing Network Version in the Same Network Envrionment
content: **List of Contents** Guideline for Installing Network Version in the Same Network Environment 1\. Check-up on HASP Driver Installation on Server PC 2\. Additional Set-up ACC Page on Client PC **Guide for Installing Network Version in the same Network Environment** **Objective** Install Network version in the same Network Environment when Server (PC connected to the red HASP Key) is unable to recognize Client (PC to run the software). **1\. Check-up on HASP Driver Installation on Server PC** **Operation** 1. Access to the Web Browser: [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/) Check Sentinel HASP Driver is installed and operating on Server as shown in the image below. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000737867/sever_1.png) 2. If the web page does not appear, reinstall Sentinel HASP Driver. [HASP Driver Install Guide ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000558507) **2\. Additional Set-up ACC Page on Client** **Operation** 1. Set up ACC page on PC you want to run the software. 2. ACC Page : [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/) 3. Click on **Configuration** (the red box in the image below). ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000737927/page_add_1.jpg) 4. Click **Access to Remote License Managers**. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000785928/page_add_2.jpg) 5. Check on 'Aggressive Search for Remote Licenses' (image below) and type the Server PC IP in "Specify Search Parameters" then click **Submit**. **※ Note:** **How to check your IP:** Windows Search ▶ Search 'Cmd.exe' ▶ Type 'ipconfig' <http://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/>[ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000737907/page_add_3.jpg) ](http://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/) 6. Wait for 10 seconds and its completed when HASP key page shows up (image below). If the page does not show up, the Server and Client may possibly be connected to different network environment. In that case, follow the link below, follow the guideline and try again. [Guideline for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000617048-%EC%9D%B8%ED%84%B0%EB%84%B7-%ED%99%98%EA%B2%BD%EC%97%90%EC%84%9C-Network-%EB%B2%84%EC%A0%84-%EC%84%A4%EC%B9%98-%EB%B0%A9%EB%B2%95) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000737887/page_add_4.png) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for troubleshooting and installing the network version of software in a shared network environment, ensuring proper connectivity between the server and client PCs.

title: [2D Tool] M:N Segment Sewing
content: **Objective** Easily sew multiple segments (M) to multiple segments (N) at once and edit them as a group. When the total length of multiple segments corresponding to M is different from the total length of multiple segments corresponding to N, N segments are divided in proportion to M segments. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Segment Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290748/M_N________.png) **M:N Segment Sewing** **※ Note:** Hold down the **Segment Sewing** tool for a while to access the **M:N Segment Sewing** tool. ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Segment Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290748/M_N________.png) **M:N Segment Sewing** 2. Click on the segments belong to M segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M sewing lines. → M sewing lines are highlighted in neon color. 3. As checking the Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on N segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. **※ Note:** * While establishing M:N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * When you click on an inappropriate segment while sewing, the segment appears in red and you cannot establish Sewing Line on the selected segment. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: The M:N Segment Sewing page provides intuitive tools for efficiently sewing and editing multiple segment pairs, ensuring proportional adjustments when segment lengths differ.
